en.headline: Legco sets up subcommittee to review tighter land records access rules
en.dek: Lawmakers endorsed a subcommittee at the House Committee meeting on Friday to examine proposed restrictions under the Land Titles Regulation after concerns from some legislators and the Journalists Association.
body: Hong Kong’s Legislative Council has agreed to establish a subcommittee to study proposed requirements and procedures for searching land records under the Land Titles Regulation.

The decision came at a House Committee meeting on Friday. It followed the government tabling eight pieces of subsidiary legislation, including the Land Titles Regulation, for negative vetting earlier in the week. Under negative vetting, the measures are gazetted first and scrutinised by lawmakers later.

The Hong Kong Journalists Association and some legislators had raised objections after the tabling. The association said the changes had not been justified and that no prior public consultation had taken place. It argued the arrangements would weaken the public’s ability to monitor the property market.

Under the proposed rules, land record searches would be limited to nine specified purposes. News reporting is not listed among them in the Chinese version of the regulation. Searches claimed to be in the public interest would require individual consideration and approval by the Land Registrar. Most provisions are expected to take effect in the first half of next year.
Currently, members of the public can search land records online after declaring compliance with privacy laws, without further restrictions on purpose.

zh.headline: 立法會成立小組委員會審議收緊土地查冊安排
zh.dek: 立法會內務委員會周五通過成立小組委員會，研究《業權規例》下擬議的土地紀錄查閱限制，此前部分議員及記者協會提出關注。
body: 香港立法會已同意成立小組委員會，研究《業權規例》下查閱土地紀錄的擬議規定及程序。
有關決定在周五的內務委員會會議上通過。政府較早前已將包括《業權規例》在內的八項附屬法例提交立法會作先訂立後審議。根據先訂立後審議程序，有關措施先刊憲，再由議員審議。
香港記者協會及部分立法會議員在法例提交後提出反對。記協指有關改動缺乏充分理據，亦未事先進行公眾諮詢，認為新安排會削弱公眾監察物業市場的能力。
根據擬議規則，土地查冊將限於九項指明目的。中文版本的規例並無將新聞報道列入其中。聲稱符合公眾利益的查冊須經土地註冊處處長個別考慮及批准。大部分條文預計於明年上半年生效。
目前，公眾人士在聲明遵守私隱法例後，即可在網上查閱土地紀錄，並無進一步的目的限制。
